conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: Can you tell me about a machine learning project you have worked on?

conversation.speaker: Candidate
conversation.text: I worked on a customer churn prediction project. I used Python and XGBoost to predict which customers were likely to cancel their subscriptions.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: Why did you choose XGBoost for this problem?

conversation.speaker: Candidate
conversation.text: I compared logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost. XGBoost produced the strongest F1 score during validation.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: Why did you use F1 score instead of accuracy?

conversation.speaker: Candidate
conversation.text: The dataset was highly imbalanced, so accuracy could be misleading. F1 score gave me a better measure of the balance between precision and recall.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: How did you handle the class imbalance?

conversation.speaker: Candidate
conversation.text: I experimented with class weights and SMOTE and compared their performance using cross-validation.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: How did you make sure SMOTE was not causing the model to overfit?

conversation.speaker: Candidate
conversation.text: I applied SMOTE only to the training folds and evaluated performance on untouched validation data. I also compared precision, recall, and F1 score across folds.
